extracted.intended_audience: offshore renewable energy developers, prospective bidders, lessees, operators, and legal/industry stakeholders (including attorneys and compliance personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed BOEM regulations governing identification of lease areas, auction procedures (PSN/FSN), bidding credits, competitive and noncompetitive lease award processes, lease/grant periods, ROW/RUE grants, and post-award administration and enforcement for offshore renewable energy activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and purpose of PSN and FSN
rubrics_metrics.description: PSN proposes procedures and provisions and invites public comment; FSN establishes the final procedures and provisions. The PSN and FSN serve as the primary sources of information for prospective bidders on the lease areas, auction procedures, and lease provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §§585.213 and 585.214 clarify and separate PSN and FSN into individual sections; BOEM uses public comments on the PSN to inform the FSN. The notices are closely related but represent distinct steps in the leasing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM authority to limit number of lease areas per party
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may set a maximum number of lease areas that an individual party may bid on or acquire in an auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule clarifies BOEM's existing authority to impose such limits; specifics would be set in the PSN/FSN for a particular auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parcel selection flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM would retain the flexibility to modify the selection of parcels offered for leasing after area identification and before the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area identification informs NEPA review and interagency consultations; BOEM may change parcel selections as needed based on environmental or other considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of area identification in NEPA and consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will use the area identification process to inform its NEPA review and associated interagency consultations to evaluate potential effects of post-lease activities on human, marine, and coastal environments and other environmental requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may develop lease stipulations or other mitigation measures and hold public hearings regarding environmental analyses after potential lease areas have been identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for assessing continued competitive interest
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may determine whether competitive interest for a lease area still exists any time before the auction when it has reason to believe competitive interest is absent, consistent with the competitive-lease-default under the OCS Lands Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.215 maintains existing process but clarifies timing flexibility; BOEM may proceed with an auction regardless of the inquiry outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credits eligibility and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.216 allows a provisional winner's bid to include the value of bidding credits awarded for demonstrable commitments that facilitate OCS renewable energy development or advance public policy (e.g., power purchase agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN and FSN would prescribe eligibility requirements, application procedures, types and values of credits; BOEM can decide not to offer credits in a given auction. Credits must be awarded in advance under FSN provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stackable vs non-stackable bidding credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidding credits may be stackable (sum of all eligible credits) or non-stackable (limited to the largest credit eligible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stackable credits incentivize bidders to meet multiple criteria; non-stackable credits limit non-monetary component of the bid. Valuation may be fixed dollar amount or percentage of cash bid as specified in FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification and timing for bidding credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualification to obtain bidding credits must be done in advance of any lease auction per FSN; qualifications may be for past actions or commitments to future actions if BOEM agrees to terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If credits are awarded for future commitments, acceptance of the lease constitutes an obligation to undertake those actions; failure to do so is noncompliance with the lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caps on bidding credits and valuation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM solicits comment on whether to codify a cap on the value of bidding credits measured as an absolute dollar amount or percentage of the bid, and on which factors should qualify for credits and how to quantify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past auctions had caps ranging 10–25% of high bid; a cap would aim to ensure a fair return to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable auction formats and award principle
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may use any auction process, including multiple factor auctions, and any procedure that is objective, fair, reasonable, and competitive; awards a lease based upon the highest total bid and provides a fair return to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.220 replaces prescriptive regulations with a flexible approach; specifics for each auction will be noticed in the PSN and finalized in the FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: General provisions applicable to all auctions
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will codify provisions and rules applicable to all auctions, including the use of the FSN to prescribe the detailed process for any auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.221 clarifies conduct and process, including BOEM's decision to conduct an auction after the Call if competitive interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances to delay, suspend, cancel, or restart an auction
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may delay, suspend, cancel, and restart an auction due to natural or man-made disaster, technical malfunction, security breach, unlawful bidding activity, administrative necessity, or any other reason BOEM determines may adversely affect fair and efficient conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may restart at whatever point it deems appropriate, reasonable, fair, and efficient, or cancel the auction in its entirety. Provision codified in proposed §585.221(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder procedural and conduct requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidders must submit bid deposits per §585.501, meet qualification requirements in §§585.106 and 585.107, and if an agent executes a lease, provide written evidence of authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.222 formalizes existing practices and cross-references qualification and deposit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on pre-auction anti-competitive communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidders are explicitly prohibited from disclosing auction strategies and economic valuations of the lease area to other bidders listed in the FSN in a way that adversely affects the United States' ability to obtain a fair return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This targets communications that could constitute explicit or tacit agreements reducing competition; does not prohibit commercial speech like public announcements of intent to participate. BOEM seeks comment on effectiveness and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental PSN/FSN information and next-best-bidder process
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.223 lists non-exhaustive supplemental auction details likely in PSN/FSN and clarifies the concept of the next highest bidder and process to determine the next best bid if provisional winner fails to meet obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Next-best-bidder criteria will be detailed in the PSN and FSN; this section provides advance notice of supplemental info but is non-exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-auction BOEM authorities and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: After an auction, BOEM may reject/accept bids, withdraw lease areas between auction completion and lease execution, and re-auction unsold areas by restarting the competitive leasing process at any reasonable step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.224 makes explicit existing practices consistent with the OCS Lands Act and BOEM's auction history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures if BOEM accepts a bid
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will refund without interest any portion of the provisional winner's bid deposit exceeding the amount due; may extend the 10-business-day deadline for provisional winner obligations; require first 12 months' rent within 45 calendar days after receipt of executed lease; winning bidder becomes such when BOEM executes the lease after appeals resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.225 updates deadlines and payment timing for flexibility (e.g., federal shutdowns/pandemics) and clarifies effective date governed by §585.237.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for provisional winner failing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional winner fails to meet obligations, BOEM may require forfeiture of bid deposit (capped at winning bid if deposit exceeds it) and take additional actions including refusal to award other leases, and referral for suspension or debarment; BOEM may select a new provisional winner by repeating the auction, selecting next best bid, or other FSN-specified criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.226 codifies potential remedies and remedies hierarchy for noncompliance after auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompetitive lease issuance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will issue a lease noncompetitively only if it determines after public notice of a proposed lease, easement, or ROW that there is no competitive interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.231 re-affirms the threshold and clarifies discretionary steps (e.g., issuing a request for information) before issuing a noncompetitive lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for information in noncompetitive process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company submits a noncompetitive lease request with the acquisition fee, BOEM may publish a request for information to determine whether others have interest; if no responses, BOEM may issue a lease noncompetitively; BOEM has discretion whether to issue such a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If BOEM elects not to issue a request for information, it will not issue a noncompetitive lease and will refund the acquisition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and sunset for DNCI in noncompetitive leasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed milestones: after DNCI publication BOEM provides fee estimate for environmental review; beneficiary has 90 calendar days to pay fee; DNCI expires within 2 years unless BOEM extends case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.231(d) and (e) create deadlines to prevent indefinite holds on noncompetitive rights; BOEM seeks comment on reasonableness of schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and statutory reviews before noncompetitive issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will conduct an environmental review of a noncompetitive lease request it intends to process and will decide whether to issue after completing environmental and other federal-law reviews (e.g., CZMA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For noncompetitive leases, CZMA concurrences will be processed pursuant to 15 CFR part 930 subpart D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renaming 'request for interest' to 'request for information' and cross-reference updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule revises nomenclature in §585.232 and elsewhere, replacing 'request for interest' with 'request for information' and updates cross-references accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and consistency changes across sections; aligns terminology used in other proposed revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restructuring commercial lease periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Rename 'terms' to 'periods'; merge preliminary and site assessment terms into a single 5-year preliminary period starting at lease effective date and ending with COP submittal or 5 years; eliminate SAP deadlines; create COP review and design & construction periods; operations period to commence at commercial operations start date and last 30 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.235 adds flexibility, aligns with elimination of SAP for met buoys, sets a 1-year limit to resolve BOEM-identified COP issues after initial submission, allows lessees to propose phased development schedules or request schedule modifications and extensions for good cause; BOEM solicits comment on timelines and on process for existing lessees to amend leases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions and phased development for commercial leases
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes expanded criteria for granting extensions of lease periods (discretion for good cause), allows lessee-proposed alternative lease period schedules for phased development, and permits modification requests when segregating or consolidating leases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows administrative flexibility and acknowledges phased development interests; extensions are subject to BOEM discretion and good-cause justification per proposed §585.235(b)-(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited lease period flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For limited leases, substitute 'period' for 'term'; operations period duration determined by BOEM prior to auction (if competitive) or negotiated (if noncompetitive); allow extensions for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.236 aligns limited leases with flexibility afforded commercial leases and ties operations period to intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW and RUE grant dimensional flexibility (PDE approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.301 removes prescribed width of ROWs to implement the Project Design Envelope (PDE) approach and clarifies that subsea cable ROWs may need to accommodate multiple associated facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical change to allow more flexible spatial definition of ROWs and consistency with proposed project easement revisions at §585.628(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification requirements for ROW/RUE applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for ROW grants and RUE grants must meet the qualifications set forth in §§585.106 and 585.107 to acquire a ROW or RUE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.302 updates cross-references; ensures applicants meet the same baseline qualification standards as lease applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW/RUE grant periods and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rename 'term' to 'period'; ROW/RUE grants will have an operations period set by BOEM (if competitive) or negotiated (if noncompetitive); preliminary period may be extended for good cause; operations period may be extended for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §585.303 aligns grants with lease-period structure and allows BOEM discretion to set duration appropriate to intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submissions for ROW/RUE requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.305 eliminates the paper copy requirement for requesting a ROW grant or RUE grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with broader move to electronic submissions per proposed §585.110 changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative streamlining of ROW/RUE processing sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidate provisions (e.g., add §585.306 provisions from existing §585.309, remove redundancy) to simplify and clarify processing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are primarily editorial to simplify subpart organization and remove redundant sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment payee update for ROW/RUE grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.316 updates the payee designation for required payments to ONRR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical correction to reflect the appropriate payee for fees and rents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalty authority for noncompliance and immediate penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.400 would expand BOEM's civil penalty authority to address a more complete range of violations, including immediate civil penalties where violations threaten serious, irreparable, or immediate harm to life, property, or the environment as authorized by section 24 of the OCS Lands Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds paragraph (f)(2) to allow immediate civil penalties like BSEE rules; civil penalties determined per 30 CFR part 550, subpart N. Aimed to allow BOEM to act without prior notice/cure period in high-risk situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of operator consistency edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical edits to ensure consistency in operator designation provisions with reorganized sections (e.g., §§585.626 and 585.645).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial alignment; no substantive change to operator designation intent but updates cross-references and numbering in proposed §585.405.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment application requirements and retention of paper copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.408 would eliminate specific elements already provided in BOEM assignment forms (BOEM-0003/0002) but would retain the paper copy requirement for assignment applications; clarifies that certain references pertain to business mergers, not lease consolidations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlines regulatory text by relying on form content while retaining some procedural requirements; proposal distinguishes mergers from consolidations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an assignment results in a segregated lease
rubrics_metrics.description: Add new §585.410 to explain circumstances under which an assignment will result in a segregated lease, adopting language from 30 CFR 556.702.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides clearer process for lessees who seek to divide leases into smaller leases for phased development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of assignment on assignor and assignee liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Renumbered §§585.411 and 585.412 clarify how assignment affects assignor and assignee liability; corrects cross-references and terminology (e.g., 'subchapter' to 'part').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial clarifications to accurately reflect regulatory liability post-assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation procedures and default harmonization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.413 establishes procedures for consolidating adjacent leases/grants, defaults to shorter remaining periods in new consolidated lease, defaults to most recently issued terms/conditions, and allows requests for modifications for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will consider and may approve requests case-by-case; will assess need to modify financial assurances before approving consolidation and may terminate any lease fully consolidated into a new lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease or grant suspension terminology update
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.415 changes 'term' to 'period' to align with lease-period nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No substantive change intended; editorial consistency across proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural corrections for suspension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §585.416 makes technical corrections and clarifications to the process for requesting a lease or grant suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/technical updates to improve clarity and cross-references; substance of suspension process retained.
